label: prf:degree-two-baryon-weight
title: Proof of degree two baryon weight
html:
Proof. Proof of degree two baryon weight

Proof sketch. The baryon has three color channels, corresponding to the three roots of the color-tube cubic. The degree-2 symmetric function \sigma_2 = \sum_{i<j} c_i c_j counts pairwise color products. The number of pairs is \binom{3}{2} = 3, which q-deforms to [3]_q = (q^3 - q^{-3})/(q - q^{-1}) at finite q.

The factor -2 arises from two sources:

  1. The sign is negative because \Phi_2 = \sum \ln|\det M_i| contributes with opposite sign to the binding energy (the determinant of the crossing matrix is -1 for all crossing types, making \Phi_2 accumulate sign information).

  2. The factor 2 is the pn crossing doubling convention: each \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n} crossing uses c = 2 (doubled to keep coefficients integral), and the \beta_2 weight compensates this doubling in the alternating channel.

At q = q_0: [3]_q \approx 3.044, giving \beta_2 \approx -6.087. The degree-2 binding scale is |\beta_2| \cdot \alpha \approx 6.09 \times 3.74 \approx 22.8 MeV, consistent with the strong-force binding energy scale. \square
